name: Tommy Boy Records
ownershipStory: Started by Tom Silverman in his own apartment with a $5,000 loan from his parents. Built into hip-hop and electro's most important independent through Afrika Bambaataa, Stetsasonic, and De La Soul, then sold to Warner Music Group in 2002. Silverman bought the label back in 2015 and still runs it independently.
hook: The apartment-sized label that put 'Planet Rock,' and electro with it, into the world.

blurb.age7: A small record company in New York that put out 'Planet Rock' and a lot of other important hip-hop and electro music.
blurb.age13: Tom Silverman started Tommy Boy with a loan from his parents and turned it into the label that released 'Planet Rock' and other foundational hip-hop and electro records. It was sold to a bigger company in 2002, and Silverman later bought it back.
blurb.adult: Tommy Boy is a clean case of an independent label built around a single scene's trust: Silverman's ear for electro and early hip-hop, and his willingness to release records other labels considered too strange, made it the commercial home for the Bronx-to-electro pipeline this dataset tracks through Bambaataa.
